readout_other: Video-EEG spike counting, status-epilepticus onset timing, spontaneous recurrent seizure counts; light/dark transition, three-chamber sociability, juvenile social interaction, and forced swim tasks
direction_notes: Pulsed US delivered at seizure onset blocked or diminished ictal EEG spikes, delayed the onset of and reduced spiking during status epilepticus, reduced spontaneous recurrent seizures in the chronic period, and improved sociability and forced-swim depressive-like behaviour.

target.label: hippocampus (transducer placed over the head just over the hippocampus, near the unilateral CA3 kainate injection site)

timing.protocol_description: Ultrasound stimulation was delivered immediately after animals began to display ictal spikes on EEG and concomitant convulsive seizure behaviours (Racine stage 4, 5, or 6) following kainate microinjection into CA3. Each 30-s stimulation used a single 1-ms pulse (5 Vpp) containing 200 acoustic cycles (0.5 Vpp) at 0.2 MHz, repeated at a PRF of 0.5 kHz; a 19-mm-diameter transducer was coupled to the head with ultrasonic gel. The number of convulsive seizures before status epilepticus differed in each mouse (6 to 30), so the number of US stimulations differed per mouse; for behavioural studies, 30-s US stimulations (without EEG recording) were given each time convulsive seizures occurred.

source_quotes.n_subjects: repeated cranial US stimulation was delivered for 5 h (KA/US group, n = 7).

flags.reason: Two separate ultrasound-exposed cohorts are reported without a combined total: n=7 mice with EEG recording (acute seizure/status-epilepticus experiment) and n=13 mice in the behaviour-only KA/US group (no EEG surgery).

The number of US stimulations per mouse varied with the number of convulsive seizures observed before status epilepticus, stated as ranging 'from 6 to 30' per mouse; no single fixed number of sessions is given.
